title: Wren and the Ember
premise: Elodie Winterbourne, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, keeps the ledgers of the Ember Guild, a hidden trade house dealing in impossible things. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, Elodie's secret becomes a death sentence, and the guild's found family must scatter or fight. Guided by a dead king's whisper, they discover the usurper is not a man but an ancient binding wearing the crown, sustained by stolen gifts like Elodie's own. In the end, Elodie unbinds the king at terrible cost—giving up their own gift—and the free cities rise, with Elodie finding belonging not in magic but in the family that stayed.
about_author: Mirabel Ishikawa is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing guild records in coastal trading cities before turning to fiction. She writes quiet fantasies about people who keep things—ledgers, secrets, and each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A day in the Ember Guild: carving a dead woman's last message into bone, balancing accounts of traded memories and bottled storms. Introduces the guild family—master Quill, apprentice Tam, fence Sera. Emotional beat: warmth and routine, with Elodie's loneliness beneath the belonging they already have.

chapters.title: What the Bones Remember
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A client brings a king's fingerbone, and inside it Elodie hears a living voice—the old king, not dead but bound, begging for help. The guild debates refusing; Quill warns that royal bones are bait. Emotional beat: dread entering a safe space; Elodie's first taste of being chosen by something larger.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Criers announce the Gift-Hunt: all gifted persons to be registered, then 'remanded.' Sera burns names from the ledger while Tam asks innocent, devastating questions. Emotional beat: fear as civic weather; the guild realizes invisibility was always a story they told themselves.

chapters.title: A Buyer with Grey Gloves
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A court agent offers gold for any bone that 'speaks,' probing the guild's stock. Elodie lies well for the first time and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: complicity and self-discovery—the hunter's logic is seductive even to the hunted.

chapters.title: Tam Runs
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Terrified by his own small gift of finding lost things, Tam flees toward the registration office, believing surrender means safety. Elodie chases him through the night market. Emotional beat: panic and tenderness; Elodie chooses Tam over safety, cementing found family.

chapters.title: The First Bonfire
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. The crown burns confiscated relics in the square; among them, gifts the guild once sold. Quill confesses to Elodie that he built the guild on a bargain he never explained. Emotional beat: guilt inherited like property; the theme of inheritance turns dark.

chapters.title: Quill's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Quill reveals the guild was founded to hide the bound king's regalia piece by piece—and that Elodie's hearing-gift descends from the first founder. Emotional beat: revelation reframing Elodie's whole life; inheritance as burden and invitation at once.

chapters.title: Salt Road South
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The guild scatters: Sera leads Elodie and Tam south toward the free cities along smugglers' salt roads, pursued by grey gloves. A checkpoint scene forces Sera to spend a precious traded favor. Emotional beat: exile's grief; home shrinks to the people beside you.

chapters.title: The Wayhouse of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Shelter at a wayhouse where hidden gifted folk trade tiny kindnesses—a warm hearth that remembers, bread that never molds. Tam learns his gift can find people, not just objects. Emotional beat: hope rekindled; community as resistance.

chapters.title: Grey Gloves at the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The court agent finds them. In the escape, the wayhouse burns and its keeper is taken. Elodie hears the dead keeper's voice join the chorus guiding them south. Emotional beat: rage and resolve; the cost of hiding becomes the cost of fighting.

chapters.title: The Free Cities
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Arrival in Meridian, jewel of the free cities, where guilds rule and the usurper's armies gather across the strait. Sera negotiates sanctuary by selling her own most guarded secret. Emotional beat: weary pragmatism; freedom has a price and she pays it quietly.

chapters.title: Council of Ledgers
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The free cities' council debates surrender versus war; Elodie presents the bound king's testimony heard through bone. Half the council calls it forgery. Emotional beat: frustration of truth without proof; Elodie steps from record-keeper to witness.

chapters.title: The Chorus Grows Louder
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Night visions: the bound king shows Elodie the binding's making—an ancient pact that ate generations of gifted souls to wear one crown. Each stolen gift strengthens the usurper. Emotional beat: horror and clarity; the hunt is harvest.

chapters.title: What Tam Found
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Using his gift, Tam locates the second regalia piece hidden beneath Meridian's tide-temple—but so do the grey gloves. A race through flooded vaults; they win the piece, barely. Emotional beat: Tam's courage blooming; the apprentice becomes essential.

chapters.title: Sera's Debt Comes Due
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The sold secret surfaces: the council arrests Sera as a collaborator to appease the crown's envoys. She refuses rescue, ordering the others to finish the work. Emotional beat: sacrifice without martyrdom; love expressed as logistics.

chapters.title: The Third Piece
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The final regalia piece lies in the usurper's camp across the strait. Quill arrives from the north with a plan and an apology, offering himself as decoy. Emotional beat: reconciliation; Quill's inherited guilt finally spent in service.

chapters.title: Across the Strait
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Smuggler's run through a blockaded strait; Quill's decoy blazes behind them. Tam finds the third piece in the usurper's own treasury, hearing it sing to his gift. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose; the found family functioning as one instrument.

chapters.title: The Throne Room of Wearing Things
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Infiltration of the palace. Elodie confronts the thing wearing the crown—it speaks in the voices of everyone Elodie has ever lost. It offers Elodie's dead mother back. Emotional beat: temptation at its cruelest; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Climax. With Tam anchoring and the dead king's chorus lending strength, Elodie carves the unbinding into the regalia bones. To sever the pact, Elodie feeds their own gift into the cut. The usurper unravels; the true king dies free at last. Emotional beat: triumph braided with loss.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Aftermath in the ruined throne room: Elodie can no longer hear the dead. The silence is vast and strange. They carry the freed king's bones home for burial. Emotional beat: mourning the magic that defined them; identity beyond the gift begins.

chapters.title: The Reckoning of Names
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Freed and pardoned, Sera rebuilds the guild's ledgers with real names instead of codes. The free cities formalize sanctuary for the gifted. Quill retires; Tam takes apprentices. Emotional beat: repair made institutional; belonging written down at last.

chapters.title: Wren and the Ember
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Epilogue. Elodie carves no more messages from the dead, but teaches young carvers ordinary craft in the guild hall. On the anniversary, a child hands Elodie a bone that hums faintly—perhaps the gift survives in new forms. Emotional beat: peace earned, legacy passed on, family chosen and kept.
